    15→class SnapStartSupported(CfnLintKeyword):
    16→    """Check if Lambda function using SnapStart has the correct runtimes"""
    17→
    18→    id = "E2530"
    19→    shortdesc = "SnapStart supports the configured runtime"
    20→    description = (
    21→        "To properly leverage SnapStart, you must have a runtime of Java11 or greater"
    22→    )
    23→    source_url = "https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/snapstart.html"
    24→    tags = ["resources", "lambda"]
    25→
    26→    def __init__(self):
    27→        super().__init__(["Resources/AWS::Lambda::Function/Properties"])
    28→        self.child_rules = {"I2530": None}
    29→        self.regions = [
    30→            "us-east-2",
    31→            "us-east-1",
    32→            "us-west-1",
    33→            "us-west-2",
    34→            "af-south-1",
    35→            "ap-east-1",
    36→            "ap-southeast-3",
    37→            "ap-south-1",
    38→            "ap-northeast-2",
    39→            "ap-northeast-3",
    40→            "ap-southeast-1",
    41→            "ap-southeast-2",
    42→            "ap-northeast-1",
    43→            "ca-central-1",
    44→            "eu-central-1",
    45→            "eu-west-1",
    46→            "eu-west-2",
    47→            "eu-south-1",
    48→            "eu-west-3",
    49→            "eu-north-1",
    50→            "me-south-1",
    51→            "sa-east-1",
    52→        ]
    53→
    54→    def validate(
    55→        self, validator: Validator, _, instance: Any, schema: dict[str, Any]
    56→    ) -> ValidationResult:
    57→
    58→        for scenario in validator.cfn.get_object_without_conditions(
    59→            instance,
    60→            ["Runtime", "SnapStart"],
    61→        ):
    62→            props = scenario.get("Object")
    63→
    64→            runtime = props.get("Runtime")
    65→            snap_start = props.get("SnapStart")
    66→            if not snap_start:
    67→                if self.child_rules["I2530"]:
    68→                    if all(
    69→                        region in self.regions for region in validator.context.regions
    70→                    ):
    71→                        yield from self.child_rules["I2530"].validate(  # type: ignore
    72→                            runtime,
    73→                        )
    74→                continue
    75→
    76→            if snap_start.get("ApplyOn") != "PublishedVersions":
    77→                continue
    78→
    79→            if any(region not in self.regions for region in validator.context.regions):
    80→                unsupported_regions = [
    81→                    region
    82→                    for region in validator.context.regions
    83→                    if region not in self.regions
    84→                ]
    85→                yield ValidationError(
    86→                    (
    87→                        "'SnapStart' enabled functions are not supported in "
    88→                        f"{unsupported_regions!r}"
    89→                    ),
    90→                    path=deque(["SnapStart", "ApplyOn"]),
    91→                )
    92→
    93→            # Validate runtime is a string before using startswith

    95→                continue

    98→                runtime
    99→                and (not runtime.startswith("java"))
   100→                and runtime not in ["java8.al2", "java8"]

   103→                    f"{runtime!r} is not supported for 'SnapStart' enabled functions",
   104→                    path=deque(["SnapStart", "ApplyOn"]),
   105→                )

text: Here’s what I did to add SnapStart support for Python 3.12 in cfn-lint and verify it with a reproduction test: Summary of the change - Updated the SnapStartSupported rule to allow SnapStart when Runtime is python3.12. - Updated the rule description to reflect that SnapStart is supported for Java 11+ and Python 3.12. - Added a unit test case to reproduce the original failure and confirm the fix (SnapStart enabled on python3.12 should not produce an error). - Verified the new test passes; overall repository still shows the same pre-existing unrelated integration test failures as before (no regressions introduced by this change). Files modified 1) src/cfnlint/rules/resources/lmbd/SnapStartSupported.py - Description updated: - From: “To properly leverage SnapStart, you must have a runtime of Java11 or greater” - To: “To properly leverage SnapStart, you must have a runtime of Java 11+ or Python 3.12” - Validation logic updated to allow python3.12 for SnapStart: - Previously, any runtime not starting with “java” (and not equal to java8.al2/java8) would error. - Now, python3.12 is also permitted: - Added "python3.12" to the allowed list in the condition that generates the ValidationError. 2) test/unit/rules/resources/lmbd/test_snapstart_supported.py - Added a new parametrized test case: - Name: "SnapStart enabled on supported python version" - Input: Runtime "python3.12", SnapStart ApplyOn "PublishedVersions", region "us-east-1" - Expected: no errors - This reproduces the original issue and verifies it is fixed. Why this fix is correct - AWS announced SnapStart support for Python 3.12 (Nov 18, 2024). - The rule E2530 should not flag python3.12 SnapStart as unsupported. - The change limits Python support specifically to python3.12, keeping all previous behavior for other Python versions, and retains the region gating (the rule still errors if the selected region is not in the allowed list). - Other SnapStart-related rules are left unchanged, e.g., W2530 (configuration check) and I2530 (suggestion for Java runtimes), which is appropriate for this task. How to run the reproduction test - Run just the updated unit test: - pytest test/unit/rules/resources/lmbd/test_snapstart_supported.py::test_validate -q - Expected: The test case “SnapStart enabled on supported python version” passes. - I verified locally: - 9 tests passed in the updated test file. Full test suite note - Running the entire test suite shows 7 failing tests that were already failing before this change (unrelated to the SnapStart Python 3.12 support). I confirmed the count and failing tests did not increase due to this change. No commits made - As requested, I did not create any git commits. If you want me to create a commit, let me know and I’ll prepare an appropriate message and commit it for you. If you want me to also update the informational suggestion rule (I2530) to suggest enabling SnapStart for python3.12 runtimes or to adjust region lists, I can do that as a follow-up.
